decisions.rationale: Tier B PASS. Q090 establishes that a safety margin extends beyond the flight area, while C001 tests the distinct source-defined quantitative boundary: use the longer of height-equivalent distance or 30m. At 50m the required reasoning changes the answer to 50m.

Explicit Chapter 6 operational-organization proposition not answer-defining elsewhere. Existing CRM and assistant questions do not test the recommendation to separate piloting and safety management by assigning a safety/operations manager.

Explicit meteorological interpretation rule: unqualified wind speed means the preceding 10-minute mean and differs from maximum instantaneous wind. Existing wind questions address vertical profile and gust timing, not this measurement definition.
Mountain/valley wind has a terrain-specific day/night reversal mechanism distinct from Q270's sea/land-breeze mechanism and calm transition periods.

Downburst/microburst scale and intensity are explicit source facts with operational hazard value. Existing thunderstorm/gust questions do not make this definition or the approximately 4km microburst boundary answer-defining.

Fixed-wing takeoff/landing into headwind and prohibition of tailwind operation because of stall risk is source-defined and distinct from existing runway-size/turn-radius and landing-speed/elevator questions.

Fixed-wing inability to hover and the resulting circular-turn holding method is an operational consequence not tested by the existing minimum-turn-radius question or B13 fixed-wing lateral-motion constraint.
Tier B PASS. Q272 tests forward climb as a power-saving technique; C008 changes the operating condition to strong downslope wind in mountain/slope flight and tests possible loss of climb capability.
Large-aircraft noise-driven route-neighborhood consideration is explicitly stated and distinct from current large-aircraft inertia/avoidance and emergency-landing-area questions.
